Hi Hiro,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — FluxPay is excited to move forward. Attached is our standard MSA (FluxPay_MSA_draft_v1.docx) and a short Exhibit A with the initial party roster. A few things we’d like to confirm up-front so we can accelerate legal review on our side: 

- Which deployment modes (hosted API vs dedicated vs private/VPC) will we need to document in the order form? FluxPay expects to start hosted and evaluate dedicated for production.
- Can Redwood provide SOC 2 / security evidence and a standard Data Processing Addendum?
- Who should be the billing contact and signatory on your side (we’ll need name, title, and company signer scope)?
- Timeline: procurement is targeting a PO within 3 weeks if redlines are straightforward.

We’ve attached ExhibitA-PartyList.xlsx that includes our primary engineering and procurement contacts. Please let us know the right Redwood contacts for contracting and security so we can route things internally.

Thanks,
Elena Suarez
Head of Platform Partnerships | FluxPay

Hi Elena — great to hear, and thanks for sending the draft. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Marcus (Solutions/Hosting) so we can get a coordinated intake.

Quick intake checklist from our side to help speed the first-pass redline: 

1) Deployment modes: note that hosted API is standard; if you expect to move to Dedicated we’ll include a clause in the order form describing reserved capacity and expected seat counts. If Private/VPC is required, that will trigger additional SOC/compliance items and lead time. Please indicate expected go-live and average qps.

2) Residency & data flows: please confirm whether any PII will be input to the model, and whether data must remain in-region. This affects the order form residency exhibit.

3) Signatory/billing: our standard signatory is a Redwood authorized officer; Marcus will confirm billing contacts and provide a signer matrix.

4) Security evidence: Kimberly, can we send them the SOC2 evidence bundle + template DPA?

Proposed next steps: 
- Kimberly to do a first-pass redline and call out any high-level non-starters (timeline: ~5-7 business days).
- Schedule a 30-min intake call for Friday to clarify hosting and residency if that works for you.

Elena — I’ll hold a tentative slot at 10:30am PT Friday; confirm and I’ll share a calendar invite.

Best,
Hiro Tanaka
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena / team — thanks for sending the MSA. I did a quick scan and flagged items to triage with FluxPay procurement/engineering. Below are the immediate asks from Legal that will materially affect our redline approach: 

- Hosting options: please confirm whether FluxPay requires a contractual commitment that production data will only be processed in a specific region (EU/US/APAC). If so, we’ll need to add an Exhibit specifying residency and operational controls.
- Security evidence: please complete the attached security collection (FluxPay_Security_Form.pdf) and provide any encryption/KMS requirements (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed).
- Insurance / liability: your MSA proposes a 10M cap and carve-outs for IP indemnity. Redwood’s standard cap is 2x fees up to $5M for commercial customers; if you require 10M please flag who owns the risk and whether there’s a preferred exceptions workflow.
- Subprocessors and data deletion: we need written confirmation on subprocessors and deletion timelines for cached prompts/KV cache.

Timeline: if we receive the security form + confirmation on region/signatory within 3 business days, we should be able to return a first-pass redline in ~5 business days. If you need a faster turnaround, please let us know which items are deal-blockers and we’ll prioritize.

Attachments: FluxPay_Security_Form.pdf (short questionnaire)

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
